title: SGLang pt loader falls back to weights_only=False for legacy tar model shards

root_cause.note: _load_pt_file first calls torch.load(weights_only=True). If the file is a legacy tar checkpoint, torch raises RuntimeError('legacy .tar format') and the code deliberately retries with weights_only=False. A model repository (or any writable model directory/PVC) can therefore ship a legacy-tar .bin whose storages entry is a pickle; the victim's model load executes it. The comment says 'trusted sources (HuggingFace Hub)', but Hub models are exactly the attacker-controlled supply-chain input.

preconditions: victim loads a model directory/PVC containing an attacker-controlled .bin/.pt shard
the shard is a legacy tar checkpoint (or is crafted to look like one)
steps: build a tar archive with a malicious pickle in the `storages` member
observe weights_only=True -> RuntimeError('legacy .tar format') and fallback weights_only=False -> pickle execution
expected_evidence: marker written from the malicious `storages` pickle
log shows the exact legacy-tar RuntimeError and the fallback call
cleanup: temp dir under evidence/ is rewritten per run
notes: Function-level reproduction of the verbatim upstream `_load_pt_file`; the rest of SGLang is not imported because the host has no GPU. The sink and fallback branch are the real 0.5.22 code.
